question: Approve the twice-revised, staff-reviewed design (delivery-bound consume + recorded merge regress verb) entering implementation; ruling includes finding 18 — is the status-set terminal guard non-bypassable even under --force (recommended, AC-2 stays absolute), or does --force keep a break-glass bypass with AC-2 narrowed to non-forced transitions?

artifacts.summary: Design: a terminal consume under a registered merge hook BINDS authority (application.state=delivering + recorded hook identity + atomic mod-block arm) instead of spending it; merge-sentinel finalize spends it atomically with terminal status + verdict + completed; delivery failure routes through merge regress (delivering->reversed, required by/at/reason, truthful optional ref, validated feedback-to routing, worktree preserved, re-entry appends successor attempt); legacy consumed-into-done entities adopted via a guarded verb; one shared OS-released flock lock + application-aware status-set terminal guard + fail-closed mod scan make done-but-undelivered unrepresentable across every terminal producer; AC-1 value-measures by driving delivery-failure-after-approval to true-done. Staff review on openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh over 3 rounds: reject (11 findings) -> reject (6) -> endorse-with-revisions (1 open: finding 18, the --force carve-out vs AC-2 absoluteness; captain rules at this gate).
